:::{#def-closed-interval}
#### Closed interval

For [real numbers](number-systems.qmd#def-real-numbers) $a \le b$,
the **closed interval** is $[a, b] \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : a \le x \le b}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-open-interval}
#### Open interval

For real numbers $a \le b$,
the **open interval** is $(a, b) \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : a < x < b}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-half-open-interval}
#### Half-open intervals

For real numbers $a \le b$,
the **half-open intervals** are $[a, b) \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : a \le x < b}$
and $(a, b] \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : a < x \le b}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-unbounded-interval}
#### Unbounded intervals

The **unbounded intervals** have at most one endpoint:

- $[a, \infty) \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : x \ge a}$
  and $(a, \infty) \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : x > a}$;
- $(-\infty, b] \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : x \le b}$
  and $(-\infty, b) \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : x < b}$;
- $(-\infty, \infty) \eqdef \reals$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-interval}
#### Interval

For real numbers $a \le b$,
the **intervals**
[@wikipedia_interval_mathematics]
with **endpoints** $a$ and $b$ are
the closed interval (@def-closed-interval),
the open interval (@def-open-interval),
and the half-open intervals (@def-half-open-interval).
The unbounded intervals (@def-unbounded-interval) have at most one endpoint.

A square bracket means the endpoint belongs to the interval,
and a parenthesis means it does not.
The symbols $\infty$ and $-\infty$ are not real numbers,
so they always get a parenthesis.

:::
